**Position Summary**

The Executive Director (ED) provides strategic leadership and overall management of the Chinese American Coalition for Compassionate Care (CACCC). The ED is responsible for advancing CACCC’s mission to promote compassionate care, advance care planning, and end-of-life care education and support for the Chinese American community.

The Executive Director works closely with the Board of Directors, staff, volunteers, healthcare professionals, community organizations, donors, and other partners to ensure the organization’s effectiveness, financial sustainability, and continued growth.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Organizational Leadership & Strategic Planning**

· Establish, implement, and evaluate education and outreach that enhance end-of-life care for Chinese American communities.

· Provide leadership and management oversight to ensure the continued success, effectiveness, and sustainability of the organization.

· Develop and implement the organization’s strategic direction and long-term strategic plans, including three-year strategic planning cycles.

· Identify new opportunities, programs, and partnerships that expand CACCC’s educational and volunteer services.

· Ensure that CACCC programs and activities are consistent with the organization’s mission, values, and strategic priorities.

**2. Program Development & Community Outreach**

· Oversee the development, implementation, and evaluation of CACCC programs and services.

· Develop and market new and existing educational resources and products promoting end-of-life care and advance care planning.

· Maintain, update, and expand CACCC’s library of culturally appropriate and translated educational materials.

· Develop and strengthen relationships with healthcare organizations, community organizations, senior-serving organizations, and other partners.

* Expand CACCC’s local, national and global outreach, visibility, and impact within the Chinese American community, the Chinese community abroad and among healthcare professionals who serve them.

**3. Fundraising & Resource Development**

· Develop and implement comprehensive funding strategies to support CACCC’s programs and operations.

· Oversee grant development and grant writing, including applications, reports, and compliance requirements.

· Cultivate relationships with existing and prospective donors, foundations, corporations, and community supporters.

· Develop and support fundraising events and other revenue-generating activities.

· Work with the Board and fundraising team to strengthen CACCC’s long-term financial sustainability.

**4. Financial & Administrative Management**

· Develop the annual organizational budget in collaboration with the Treasurer and Board of Directors.

· Monitor organizational expenses and ensure responsible stewardship of CACCC resources.

· Ensure appropriate administrative systems, policies, and procedures are in place to support effective operations.

**5. Staff & Volunteer Management**

· Recruit, hire, develop, supervise, and evaluate staff as needed.

· Provide leadership and support to staff and volunteers to ensure effective implementation of CACCC programs and operations.

· Establish clear responsibilities, goals, and performance expectations.

· Foster a collaborative, respectful, and mission-driven organizational culture.

· Support volunteer recruitment, engagement, training, and development.

**6. Board Relations & Governance**

· Coordinate and facilitate quarterly Board of Directors meetings.

· Prepare and present the Executive Director’s report covering past, current, and upcoming activities, new initiatives, program developments, and organizational priorities.

· Provide quarterly financial updates in collaboration with the Treasurer.

· Keep the Board informed about current and emerging end-of-life care initiatives, policies, legislation, and community needs.

· Provide ongoing education and relevant information to the Board regarding developments in end-of-life care, advance care planning, hospice, palliative care, caregiver support, and related issues.

· Direct, support, and collaborate with Board members serving on CACCC committees and task forces.

· Carry out Board-approved policies, decisions, and strategic priorities.

**7. Public Relations & Community Representation**

· Represent CACCC in a dignified, knowledgeable, and professional manner to the media, healthcare community, donors, partners, and the public.

· Serve as a spokesperson and advocate for CACCC’s mission and programs.

· Participate in community events, conferences, health fairs, educational programs, and professional meetings.

· Maintain current knowledge of legislation, policies, and emerging issues affecting end-of-life care and advance care planning.

· Promote CACCC’s work through community outreach, partnerships, public presentations, and other appropriate communication channels.

**Qualifications**

· Candidates **must currently reside in California** or have a confirmed permanent California address prior to their official start date to ensure compliance with state payroll, tax, and labor laws. Must have a current and valid passport.

· Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree preferred, particularly in healthcare.

· 3–5 years of management or leadership experience in a nonprofit organization preferred.

· Knowledge and experience in hospice, palliative care, end-of-life care, advance care planning, or related healthcare services preferred.

· Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and public-speaking skills.

· Bilingual fluency in English and Mandarin or Cantonese strongly preferred.

· Strong organizational, financial management, and strategic planning skills.

· Ability to build and maintain effective relationships with staff, donors, healthcare professionals, community organizations, volunteers, and other stakeholders.

jobs.description:
**The Organization**

The Mental Health Client Action Network (MHCAN) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization dedicated to supporting adults in Santa Cruz County with lived experience of mental health challenges. Founded nearly 40 years ago as an independent peer support center, MHCAN is actively transitioning its operational framework to an accredited Clubhouse Model of Services.

In alignment with Clubhouse standards, MHCAN operates as a member-driven community where participants ("members") and staff work side-by-side to run daily center operations, build social connections, and pursue employment, education, and wellness goals. All MHCAN staff members share lived experience with a mental health condition and/or navigating the mental health system.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of MHCAN and is responsible for providing strategic leadership, operational oversight, program management, community engagement, and resource development. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director ensures the organization stays true to its core mission of peer empowerment while successfully guiding the agency through its transition to the Clubhouse model and maintaining strong alignment with County Behavioral Health.

This is a full-time (1.0 FTE / 40 hours per week) exempt position.

**Compensation:** $95,000 – $105,000 annually, depending on experience.

**Core Responsibilities**

**Human Resources & Staff Leadership (25%)**

* Hire, train, supervise, and mentor all program staff and peer support team members.
* Foster a positive, supportive, and accountable organizational culture centered on lived experience and recovery.
* Manage staff scheduling, performance evaluations, and team development.
* Partner with the Fiscal Agent (FSAS) on HR policy enforcement, workplace safety, and personnel administration.

**Program Oversight & Clubhouse Model Transition (25%)**

* Lead the agency’s transition to and ongoing operation of a certified Clubhouse model of services.
* Ensure daily program activities effectively meet client needs and contract objectives.
* Evaluate program outcomes and implement continuous service delivery improvements.
* Monitor compliance with grant deliverables and County service agreements.

**Organizational Leadership & Strategy (20%)**

* Implement the organization's mission, vision, and strategic goals, serving as a passionate advocate for peer support.
* Develop annual organizational objectives in close collaboration with the Board of Directors and the County contract monitor.
* Ensure organizational compliance with all applicable legal and nonprofit regulatory standards.
* Provide monthly performance, operational, and financial reports to the Board.

**Community Relations & County Partnership (15%)**

* Serve as the primary spokesperson and public representative for MHCAN.
* Build and maintain productive, collaborative relationships with County Behavioral Health, local community partners, and contracted service providers.
* Represent MHCAN in local task forces, community meetings, and mental health advocacy networks.

**Fundraising & Resource Development (10%)**

* Research, write, and manage grant applications to diversify funding streams.
* Cultivate relationships with individual donors, private foundations, and community partners.
* Oversee donor stewardship and track grant reporting deadlines.

**Financial Oversight & Fiscal Agent Coordination (5%)**

* Develop and manage the annual operating budget (approximately $590,000) in partnership with the Board and Fiscal Agent.
* Collaborate directly with Front St. Administrative Services to oversee fiduciary practices, review monthly financial statements, and ensure budget alignment. *(Note: Daily bookkeeping, payroll processing, and accounting entries are performed directly by the Fiscal Agent.)*

  

**Qualifications**

* **Lived Experience:** Lived experience as a person with a mental health condition and/or direct experience navigating the mental health system is required.
* **Education & Experience:** Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience.
* **Leadership Experience:** Minimum 2–3 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in a nonprofit or community service environment.
* **Management & Budgeting:** Demonstrated experience supervising staff, managing program operations, and overseeing grant/contract deliverables.
* **Skills:** Strong communication, interpersonal, and project management skills with the ability to build consensus across diverse community stakeholders.

**Performance Expectations**

* Maintain a balanced annual budget in coordination with the Fiscal Agent.
* Ensure successful transition and operational implementation of the Clubhouse model.
* Provide consistent leadership, accountability, and support to program staff.
* Maintain strong, transparent relationships with the Board of Directors, County Behavioral Health, and community partners.
* Ensure timely completion of grant reports and contract deliverables.

**Working Conditions & Physical Requirements**

* Standard office environment with high levels of interpersonal interaction.
* Computer and telephone usage for extended periods.
* Occasional evening or weekend attendance at Board meetings or community events.
* Local travel within Santa Cruz County.
* Ability to lift up to 25 pounds occasionally.

**Reporting Relationship:** Reports directly to the MHCAN Board of Directors.

**About the Authority**

The Trinity River Authority of Texas was created by the Legislature in 1955 as a conservation and reclamation district. Its mission is to promote conservation, reclamation, protection, and development of the natural resources of the Trinity River basin for the benefit of the public. Its vision is to promote the natural, economic, and recreational benefits of the Trinity River as the foundation for future generations. Core values are Integrity, Accountability, and Service.

TRA is the largest river authority in Texas and the largest wholesale provider of wastewater treatment services in the state. It owns and operates four regional water treatment facilities and five regional wastewater treatment facilities, operates the Lake Livingston Dam, manages water sales from four reservoirs, and operate and oversee multiple recreation facilities around Lake Livingston. The Authority is self-supporting. It receives no ad valorem taxes, sales taxes, or annual state appropriations. Each operating project is an independent financial entity, funded by the customers that contract for its services. **Organization Overview**

**Founded in 1951 by Corning Incorporated as a gift to the nation, the Corning Museum of Glass (CMoG) is the global center for the art, science, and history of glass.** The Museum shapes the understanding and appreciation of glass worldwide and draws more than 300,000 visitors each year to a city of roughly 10,000 residents. The *New York Times* named CMoG as one of the U.S. museums to see in 2025, and *Newsweek* readers voted CMoG one of the Top 3 Best Art Museums in America.

With more than 10,000 works on display, the Museum galleries showcase glass selected from a permanent collection of more than 50,000 objects representing more than 3,500 years of history. The expansive collection is presented in three core galleries – 35 Centuries of Glass, Heineman, and Contemporary Art & Design – to tell the global story of glass from antiquity through the present day. The Innovation Galleries highlight scientific and technological achievements using glass, ranging from casserole dishes to telescopes to optical fiber.

**CMoG is regarded as the conservation authority on glass to museums and institutions around the world.**

In late 2024, the Museum celebrated the expansion of The Studio, funded primarily by a successful capital campaign. The Studio, which is celebrating its 30th anniversary in 2026, features the first large scale kiln casting facility in North America and can support over 100,000 Make Your Own Glass projects annually. The state-of-the-art facilities provide artists and students with the tools and the support they need to take risks and make discoveries; opportunities for people of all skill levels to forge and deepen their understanding of glass; and connections to the glass community, where artists gather to create, learn, and share.

**Role Summary & Context for Recruitment**

The Chief Development Officer (CDO) is responsible for the strategic planning, management, and success of the comprehensive fundraising efforts of the Corning Museum of Glass, including the pursuit of long-term relationships that benefit the financial health of the Museum. The CDO oversees policy, strategy, and execution of the work of the Development Department, which includes individual and planned giving, corporate, foundation and government giving, membership, giving appeals, special events, and donor relations programs. This leader reports to the Museum President and Executive Director, providing them with expert advice on all aspects of fundraising, including policy development and changes as well as new program directions. The CDO will manage all future campaigns. The CDO works closely with the Development Committee and Board of Trustees to build the Museum’s visibility, impact, and financial resources. The CDO serves as a champion for CMoG and the catalyst in strengthening the Museum’s culture of philanthropy.

The CDO oversees a team of seven staff members and provides strategic oversight and leadership for the Development Department’s annual operating budget.

Formal fundraising at CMoG is a relatively young discipline, having taken shape over the past decade alongside the Museum's landmark expansion of The Studio, and its successful capital campaign. As CMoG enters its next chapter, the Museum is investing in building a comprehensive, professionalized development program capable of matching the global stature of its collection, scholarship, and artistic community. Description
  

Indiana Tech is a thriving, independent, teaching-oriented university that delivers career-oriented programming in a wide variety of disciplines that includes business, engineering, computer sciences, criminal justice, cybersecurity, marketing, health sciences, communication and helping professions. Indiana Tech enrolls nearly 1,500 students in its traditional undergraduate programs on its picturesque main campus, and nearly 5,000 students in its adult and online program. We offer degrees at the associate, bachelor’s, master's, and doctoral levels and undergraduate and graduate certificates.

Over 41% of our students are either globally or domestically diverse; this contributes to our unique vibrant and inclusive campus community. All academic programs are designed to provide students with relevant and practical experiences, including an emphasis on internships. The university is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission.

Indiana Tech is committed to fostering a welcoming and respectful environment for all. We actively support the recruitment, engagement, and retention of students, faculty, and staff from a wide range of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We believe that creating a sense of connection and support across our campus community plays an essential role in preparing students to succeed and contribute in a global society.

Indiana Tech has big plans for its future. Learn more at Indiana Tech Strategic Plan or strategicplan.indianatech.edu .

Indiana Tech is seeking a visionary, collaborative, and results-driven leader to serve as its Executive Director of the AI Institute. Reporting to the Vice President for Academic Affairs, the Executive Director will provide strategic vision and operational leadership for Indiana Tech’s AI Institute. This position will build a coordinated pathway that moves faculty, staff, and students from AI awareness to hands-on curriculum redesign while positioning Indiana Tech as a regional leader in the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence in higher education.

The Executive Director will establish the Institute’s strategic vision, annual priorities, and multi-year roadmap in alignment with Indiana Tech’s Strategic Plan and the AIHE grant. This leader will oversee the Institute’s faculty AI-development pipeline, spanning awareness, coaching, and curriculum execution, and will supervise a multidisciplinary team responsible for AI readiness, faculty strategy, curriculum design and integration, regional partnerships, and intelligent institutional operations

The Executive Director will serve as principal administrator for the AIHE grant, with responsibility for budget oversight, milestone tracking, funder reporting, and renewal or expansion proposals. This position will also oversee the Institute’s operating and grant budgets and establish shared metrics and reporting tools that clearly communicate progress across the AI-development pipeline.

As the Institute’s principal liaison to the University AI Council, the Executive Director will ensure that programs, tools, and data practices align with Indiana Tech’s Artificial Intelligence Policy and applicable FERPA, GLBA, and data-governance obligations. This leader will convene and chair an AI Institute Advisory Board composed of academic deans, faculty, Information Technology, and Human Resources representatives to establish priorities and review new AI tools before campus-wide implementation.

The Executive Director will build regional employer and community partnerships, represent the AI Institute to grantors, accreditors, and external funders, and monitor the national AI-in-higher-education landscape to inform institutional priorities. Additional responsibilities include leading change-management and communication efforts, publishing an annual “State of AI at Indiana Tech” report, sponsoring a faculty AI fellows or seed-grant program, and supporting the hiring, onboarding, and performance management of Institute employees.

**Required Skills and Experience**

The successful candidate will possess a master’s degree in higher education administration, educational technology, computer science, artificial intelligence, business, or a related field. Candidates must have at least seven years of progressively responsible leadership experience in higher education, including experience supervising professional staff and managing budgets and personnel.

Candidates must demonstrate a strong understanding of generative AI technologies, their applications in higher education, and the related risks and compliance considerations, including FERPA, GLBA, and data governance. The position requires the ability to balance innovation with responsible technology adoption and to translate complex technical, academic, and compliance matters for varied institutional audiences.

Experience administering grant-funded programs, including budget oversight and funder reporting, is required. Candidates must also have experience developing partnerships with external organizations, such as employers, community organizations, or regional and national networks.

The successful candidate will possess outstanding written, verbal, and executive presentation skills and be prepared to represent Indiana Tech with external partners and interested parties. Candidates must demonstrate the ability to build consensus and advance complex initiatives across academic and administrative units with competing priorities.

**Preferred Skills and Experience**

A doctoral degree in higher education administration, educational technology, computer science, artificial intelligence, business, or a related field is preferred.

Preferred candidates will have experience leading institutional AI, educational technology, or digital-transformation initiatives. Experience working with or reporting to institutional governance and policy bodies, such as data-governance or AI-governance committees, is also preferred.
